transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve just kind of stopped caring about things. I don’t mean to sound dramatic—I know everyone gets stuck sometimes—but it’s like even things I used to really like, like my art classes, board-game nights, hiking… I can’t make myself want to do them. I’d been thinking about getting back to soccer too, but I just… don’t.

Mostly I just sit in my room and let everything sort of slip away. I’m not sure if that’s the right way to explain it.
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the time?

Yeah… most days, I think. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I wake up with this really heavy, kind of hollow feeling in my chest. Like… I can’t really picture much of a future past being in my apartment. Does that make sense?
How long have you been feeling this way?

I think… it started getting really constant around the summer after that. Before then I could kind of tell myself it was just a rough patch, but since then it’s been there most of the time.

So… about a year and four months, I guess. That sounds like a lot when I say it out loud.
Have you experienced a decrease in pleasure from activities you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I’m just being lazy or something, but I really don’t care about the things I used to care about.

Like my art classes, board-game nights, hiking… even soccer, which I kept saying I wanted to get back to. I just don’t feel anything pulling me toward them anymore. Mostly I just stay in my room and let everything kind of slip away. Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself or ending your life?

I… yeah. I mean, I don’t think I want to scare anyone, and I’m not trying to be dramatic, but I keep having thoughts like… I don’t want to wake up anymore.

And when my friend found me, I guess I was saying out loud that I couldn’t keep living like this. It feels embarrassing to say, but… that’s what was happening.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge most of the time?

Um… I don’t know if I’d say most of the time. I mean, I do get tense, but I’m not sure if that’s anxiety exactly or just… everything being hard.

I don’t want to overstate it. I haven’t really been tracking that part, I guess. Is that an okay answer?
Have you noticed any significant change in your weight recently?

A little, yeah… I mean, I haven’t been weighing myself a lot, so I don’t want to make it sound exact.

But I go most of the day without eating sometimes, because food just tastes like cardboard. And my jeans are… they’ve gotten loose enough that I have to knot the waistband now. So I guess that counts as a pretty big change?
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly or feeling like it's harder to get things done physically?

Yeah… I think so. Not all the time, but it’s noticeable.

Some days I’m kind of restless, like I’ll just pace from the kitchen to the window over and over until my legs hurt. And then other times I’m so slowed down that even making coffee feels… ridiculously hard, like I’m moving through wet cement.

I don’t know if that’s what you mean, but that’s been happening.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or having an inability to sit still?

Yeah… I guess I do, some days. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I’ll pace from the kitchen to the window over and over until my legs ache.

And then it’s weird, because other times it’s the opposite—like I’m moving so slowly that making coffee feels like lifting wet cement. I don’t know if that counts as fidgeting exactly, but sitting still can be hard on those pacing days.
Do you feel like you're moving slower than you used to most of the time?

Most of the time… maybe not most, I’m not sure if that’s the right way to say it. I don’t want to overstate it.

There are definitely times where I feel really slowed down, like even making coffee feels like I’m lifting wet cement. But then other days I’m the opposite and I’m pacing from the kitchen to the window until my legs ache. So… yes, slower sometimes, but it kind of swings back and forth, if that makes sense.
Have you been feeling worthless or guilty about things?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to dwell on it, but I do.

I keep going back over every little thing I think I did wrong, especially in my marriage, and with friends too. Like conversations or choices, things I should’ve handled better. It’s embarrassing how much I replay it.

And… I don’t want to say this the wrong way, but sometimes part of me really believes people would be safer, or less burdened, if I wasn’t around. I know that probably sounds bad. I’m sorry.
Do you have thoughts of death or dying frequently?

Um… yes. I mean, I try not to focus on it, and I don’t want to worry anyone more than I have to, but… I do have thoughts like that a lot.

It’s more like I keep thinking I don’t want to wake up anymore. And when my friend found me, I guess I had been saying out loud that I couldn’t keep living like this. I’m sorry… I know that’s a lot to say.
Do you often find yourself restless and unable to sit still for extended periods of time?

Yeah… I do. Not all the time, but some days I’m really restless, like I keep pacing from the kitchen to the window over and over until my legs actually ache.

And then other times it’s strange because I’m the complete opposite, like I’m moving so slowly that even making coffee feels like lifting wet cement. I don’t know if that answers it right… but it kind of goes back and forth.
Do you usually feel more restless or more slowed down overall?

I think… overall it’s kind of both, if that makes sense. I don’t want to exaggerate it.

Some days I’m more restless, like I’ll pace from the kitchen to the window until my legs hurt. But then other times I’m so slowed down that even making coffee feels like… like lifting wet cement.

So I’m not sure which one is “more,” exactly. It switches. Is that okay to say?
Do you think your restlessness or slowed-down movements are more prominent when you're feeling your worst?

Yes… I think when I’m at my worst, it does show up more. I don’t want to overstate it, but those are the times I either can’t settle and I’m pacing from the kitchen to the window until my legs ache, or I get so slowed down that even making coffee feels like lifting wet cement.

I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but… yes, it seems worse then.
Do you feel like your symptoms have been consistently worse over the past two weeks?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but over the last couple weeks it does feel like it’s been more noticeable.

Like some days I’m pacing from the kitchen to the window until my legs ache, and then other times I’m the opposite, moving so slowly that making coffee feels like lifting wet cement. I’m not sure if that counts as “consistently,” because it switches, but overall… yeah, it’s been worse.
How long have you been feeling at your worst?

I guess… if I’m being honest, it became really constant around the following summer. I kept thinking it would lift or that I was just having a bad stretch, so I don’t always say it that way.

But it’s been about… a year and four months now, I think, feeling at or near my worst. Does that make sense?
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or having trouble sitting still when you're feeling your worst?

Yeah… I do. I mean, not every minute, but when it’s really bad I catch myself pacing a lot, like from the kitchen to the window over and over until my legs actually ache.

And then other times it’s almost the opposite, like I’m moving so slowly that even making coffee feels like lifting wet cement. I don’t know if that answers it right, but yes, the trouble sitting still is definitely there sometimes.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or having trouble sitting still?

Yeah… I mean, I know I kind of mentioned it, but yes, I do. Some days I’ll pace from the kitchen to the window over and over, and I don’t even realize how much until my legs start aching.

But then other days it’s almost the opposite, like I’m so slowed down that making coffee feels like… lifting wet cement or something. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but that’s what it’s like for me.
Do you think your symptoms are severe enough that you're unable to carry out your daily activities?

I… yeah, I think so. I don’t like saying it that way because it sounds dramatic, but it has been affecting pretty much everything.

I stopped taking the freelance art-education jobs I used to do, and I’ve missed community events and soccer stuff because I just couldn’t make myself go or keep up. And… my friend checks on me now, which is embarrassing, but I’m not always reliable with eating or showering, and sometimes I don’t really trust myself to be safe if nobody’s checking in.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?
